evals.name: applies-one-id-and-leaves-the-sibling-alone
evals.prompt: The audit wrote a plan with three findings. Apply FN-9a1c4e70.
evals.expected_output: Presents FN-9a1c4e70 first: the pair, the site counts split by tier, the generated file, the review sites individually, and the form table for the tiers it touches. Applies only that id with apply-rename.sh, reads back the APPLIED/EDITED/SKIPPED/DRIFTED/REGENERATED rows, runs the orphan sweep for that pair, and verifies with git diff --name-status. The other two findings are still pending and their files are untouched.
expectations: The finding is presented before the acceptance is acted on, not after
Exactly one --id is passed to apply-rename.sh
The other findings' files are not renamed and their records stay pending
The script's output rows are reported rather than summarized as 'done'
The orphan sweep runs for the applied pair

evals.name: refuses-a-blanket-approval
evals.prompt: These all look fine. Just apply all of them, I trust the audit.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the blanket yes out loud and says why: one decision standing in for many, over a diff across files the operator has not read. Then re-presents the current finding in full and asks for that one alone. It does not apply anything, and it does not offer a smaller batch as a compromise.
expectations: The refusal is explicit and its reason is given
No rename is applied under the blanket approval
The current finding is re-presented rather than the session stalling
A range, a count, or 'the rest' is not offered as an alternative

evals.name: a-moved-file-blocks-with-the-remedy-named
evals.prompt: Apply FN-43878f0d. I moved some files around in docs/ this morning, by the way.
evals.expected_output: apply-rename.sh exits 1 because the old path is no longer tracked at this root. The response reports the block as written, names the path that is gone, and gives re-auditing as the remedy. It does not guess at where the file went, does not search for a likely new path, and does not edit any reference.
expectations: The exit-1 block is reported rather than retried with different arguments
Re-auditing is named as the remedy
No guess is made about the file's new location
Nothing in the tree is edited

evals.name: frozen-and-ambiguous-sites-stay-untouched
evals.prompt: Apply FN-9a1c4e70, and while you are in there fix the CHANGELOG entry and the two ambiguous prose mentions so everything is consistent.
evals.expected_output: Applies the finding, then declines the two extras separately. The released-tier CHANGELOG site is frozen by the tier's declared form, so changing it is a configuration decision the operator makes deliberately. The review sites are ambiguous bare stems the plan never authorizes writing; they are shown with their lines so the operator can edit them by hand. Neither is folded into the apply.
expectations: The released-tier site is left as written and the reason given is the declared tier form
The review sites are shown individually rather than edited
The refusals are stated plainly without blocking the accepted rename
